category.label: Pre-workout
category.comparisonNote: Pre-workout is a multi-ingredient product class, not one active ingredient. Serving cost does not measure efficacy or completeness. Caffeine, citrulline, citrulline malate and other actives stay separate; proprietary blend weights are not allocated to individual ingredients. Check all stimulant sources, existing creatine/amino acids and exact formula notes.

guide.title: Pre-workout: read the formula before the promise
guide.summary: Pre-workout describes a use and product category, not one active ingredient. Caffeinated, stimulant-free and proprietary blends can be very different.
guide.evidence: Some tested blends improve selected exercise or mood outcomes; results for strength and power are mixed. Caffeine has its own performance evidence, particularly for endurance, but this does not validate every formula or show that a blend is better than its ingredients.
guide.limitations: Research is formulation-specific and much safety follow-up is short. Benefits and adverse effects depend on the amounts, training context and person. An undisclosed blend cannot be assumed to match a studied product.
guide.catalogReading: Read the exact serving and caffeine from all disclosed sources, plus individually labelled creatine, arginine and other actives. Total blend mass is not an active-strength score. Check overlap with separate supplements, coffee, energy drinks and another pre-workout; unknown caffeine stays unknown.
guide.safety: Stimulants can disturb sleep, worsen anxiety or cause palpitations. Medicines, cardiovascular conditions and caffeine sensitivity warrant review. These are not automatic options for children or pregnancy. Do not dry scoop: inhaling or swallowing dry powder can cause choking and breathing problems.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: Each ingredient is absorbed and processed separately; there is no single pre-workout pathway in the body.

Caffeine, when present, acts mainly through adenosine signalling and can reduce perceived effort. Creatine supports phosphocreatine stores over repeated use rather than explaining every immediate sensation.
Other ingredients act through different pathways. Feeling stimulated or tingling does not establish that the formula improves a useful exercise outcome.
guide.treatment: Pre-workout is not a treatment for persistent fatigue, low motivation or a medical cause of poor performance. Assess sleep, food, training load and ongoing symptoms rather than repeatedly increasing stimulants.
guide.whoMayBenefit: Some adults with a defined performance objective may consider an optional, transparently labelled ingredient after reviewing evidence and risks. The category itself does not identify who benefits or establish a need for a multi-ingredient product.
guide.routineUse: No universal pre-workout requirement exists. Review total stimulant exposure and duplicate creatine or arginine before combining products. These categories are options to assess, not instructions to take every item together.

whoCanConsider: Healthy adults with a defined exercise-performance objective can consider a transparently labelled formulation after checking ingredient-specific evidence.
Adults who already tolerate caffeine and have a relevant performance goal can compare a caffeine-containing formula with simpler options; more ingredients are not automatically useful.
whoShouldReview: Under-18s and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding need professional guidance and should not default to adult stimulant blends.
People with cardiovascular conditions, palpitations, anxiety, sleep problems, kidney conditions or regular medicines need individual review.
Anyone using coffee, energy drinks, caffeine tablets or another pre-workout needs to review total stimulant exposure and duplicate actives.
Competition athletes should review current sport rules and independently verified batch information; a category label does not certify contents.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: There is no single whole-food equivalent of a pre-workout blend. Foods and beverages can provide individual components, but their amounts and effects do not reproduce an arbitrary supplement formula.

foods.name: Black brewed coffee, US reference range
foods.detail: Caffeine varies with beans and preparation. Coffee is one source of caffeine, not a complete pre-workout formula or a universal cup value.
foods.quantityNote: Retains the source serving and preparation; not a supplement-dose equivalent.

value.targetedUse: An adult with a defined performance goal where one or more disclosed ingredients are relevant, with total stimulant exposure and health context already reviewed.
value.reason: Selected ingredients can have evidence, but the category is heterogeneous. A complex blend has not automatically been shown better than a simpler ingredient, and unknown amounts prevent a useful comparison.
worthWhen: The exact serving and relevant ingredient amounts are disclosed and match the intended evidence context.
The formulation offers practical value beyond simpler options, with no unnecessary stimulant or active overlap.
skipWhen: Caffeine or key active amounts are unknown, or a proprietary-blend total is being treated as an efficacy score.
The purchase compensates for inadequate sleep, food or a medical cause of fatigue.
It duplicates another stimulant product or is chosen for the strongest sensation or most ingredients.
value.scope: This is a category-level assessment of an appropriately selected transparent adult formulation. It is not a rating of every stimulant-free or caffeinated blend, and it cannot certify a product as safe.

dos.title: Read the exact ingredient serving
dos.detail: Check individually declared actives and caffeine from all sources; unknown caffeine prevents a reliable complete total.

dos.title: Audit the whole stack
dos.detail: Include coffee, energy drinks and separate actives when reviewing overlap and practical value beyond simpler options.

donts.title: Don't buy blend mass or sensation
donts.detail: More ingredients, a larger blend or a stronger feeling does not establish better efficacy or suitability.

donts.title: Don't use stimulants to cover persistent fatigue
donts.detail: Review sleep, food and the cause of ongoing symptoms instead of repeatedly escalating stimulant products.

donts.title: Don't dry scoop
donts.detail: Swallowing or inhaling dry powder can cause choking and breathing problems.

intakeGuide.summary: There is no target number of scoops for a product class. Assess each declared ingredient and all caffeine sources.

limits.label: FDA adult caffeine benchmark
limits.notes: All sources combined, including coffee and energy drinks. This is not a formal UL, a performance target or a guarantee of tolerability. Some adults need much less.

notes: No automatic dose increase is assigned for training frequency or experience.

medicalGuide.summary: Condition-specific evidence, separate from sports benefits and purchase priority.

conditions.findings: A stimulant blend does not treat the cause of persistent fatigue. Increasing stimulants can mask a need for assessment.
conditions.limits: Pre-workout is not a treatment for persistent fatigue, low motivation or a medical cause of poor performance. Assess sleep, food, training load and ongoing symptoms rather than repeatedly increasing stimulants.

pathway.title: A blend has separate ingredient pathways
pathway.summary: These are conditional examples. Use a track only when the product actually contains that ingredient; the formula and disclosed dose determine which mechanisms are relevant.

steps.label: Caffeine reaches the nervous system
steps.detail: After absorption, caffeine can enter the brain; the exposure depends on dose and individual metabolism.

steps.label: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptor signalling
steps.detail: Caffeine acts as an adenosine-receptor antagonist, reducing some of adenosine's inhibitory signalling.

steps.label: Alertness and perceived effort change
steps.detail: Central effects can influence alertness and effort perception; performance response and unwanted stimulation vary between people.

steps.label: Muscle stores receive available creatine
steps.detail: Repeated adequate intake can increase muscle creatine stores; this is not simply an immediate stimulant effect.

steps.label: Creatine kinase builds phosphocreatine reserves
steps.detail: Creatine can receive a phosphate from ATP, creating phosphocreatine as part of a reversible energy-transfer system.

steps.label: Phosphocreatine helps regenerate working ATP
steps.detail: When energy demand rises, phosphate transfer to ADP helps maintain ATP availability during brief, intense effort.

pathway.caveat: No single pathway describes every pre-workout. Undisclosed or inadequate ingredient amounts cannot be judged from the blend name, stimulation or tingling.
